complexity.correctness_reason: decode and encode recurse once per node, so any list longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 nodes) raises RecursionError; NeetCode's cap of 100 nodes per list keeps this from triggering.
complexity.notes: Decoding into one big integer changes the cost model: each level of decode multiplies an O(k)-digit number by 10, so the whole decode is O(n^2) digit work instead of O(n), and encode's repeated //10 is likewise quadratic. A single pass ||building the result digit by digit with a running carry|| (as your previous submission did) is O(n) and iterative. Both helpers also recurse once per node, which is what limits how large an input this can handle. Minor: encode relies on an implicit None return for n == 0, which happens to be exactly the base case needed, but the top-level `if a+b else ListNode(0)` guard is easy to misread as dead code.
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes each list into a single Python integer (place value via 10 * decode(next)), adds the two integers, and recursively re-encodes the sum into a list, with a special case for a sum of zero.
